profile.name: Karikázó
profile.tagline: A traditional Hungarian women's circle dance performed to a cappella singing.
profile.insight: Karikázó, a medieval-rooted circle dance for women, serves as a rhythmic bridge during dance events or as entertainment during periods when instrumental music is forbidden.
profile.profile: Karikázó is a traditional Hungarian circle dance performed exclusively by women. Rooted in the medieval stratum of European folk traditions, it is characterized by unison singing rather than instrumental accompaniment. While once more prominent, it now frequently serves as an interlude during larger dance events or as a primary form of entertainment during fasting periods when instrumental music is restricted.
profile.profile_long: Karikázó is a traditional Hungarian circle dance performed exclusively by women. It belongs to the 'old stratum' of Hungarian folk dance, a category of dances attested to in sources before the 18th century and presumed to have roots in the Middle Ages. The dance is characterized by its simplicity and its reliance on vocal performance rather than instrumental music. The dancers move in a circle, performing a series of simple motifs, while singing folksongs in unison. This form of dance is most popular in the Transdanubia region. Historically, the karikázó served as a vital form of entertainment during periods of fasting when instrumental music and dance were prohibited. In contemporary settings, it often functions as an interlude during larger dance events, filling the intervals between more complex couple or male dances. While some of its motifs bear a resemblance to those found in Faroese dances, the karikázó remains a distinct element of the Hungarian folk tradition. Due to the rise of other dance forms over time, the karikázó has been pushed to the periphery of the folk dance repertoire, though it remains a recognized and practiced part of the Hungarian dance heritage.

sections.origins_and_history: The karikázó is part of the old stratum of Hungarian folk dances, which are attested to in sources before the 18th century and are presumed to go back to the Middle Ages. It is closely connected with medieval European circle dances.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance is performed in a circle by women only. It consists of a few simple motifs, with the primary focus on the singing, which is performed by all women in unison.
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance is accompanied by the singing of folksongs rather than instrumental music. The singing is done by all women in unison.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance serves as entertainment in periods of fasting when dance and music are restricted, and as an interval filler during dance events.
sections.regional_variants: The dance is most popular in Transdanubia.
sections.lineage: It is closely connected with medieval European circle dances.

claims.text: The old stratum comprises dances attested to in sources before the 18th century and are presumed to go back to the Middle Ages. This group, which includes types such as the Karikázó, Ugrós, Legényes and many others, shares connections with medieval dance forms found throughout Europe.
